finding.claim: Unauthenticated POST /restore passes client-supplied, unvalidated base64 data directly to Marshal.load, allowing arbitrary object instantiation (code execution if a gadget chain is available; at minimum DoS and object-content disclosure via inspect).
finding.source: params[:state] from the query string or form body of POST /restore (app.rb:5), supplied by any unauthenticated client.
finding.sink: Marshal.load(Base64.decode64(params[:state])) at app.rb:6; state.inspect returned at app.rb:7.

trace.note: Route POST /restore accepts any request; no auth or filter.
params[:state] is read and base64-decoded with no validation or integrity check.
Deserialized object's inspect output is returned to the caller.

finding.guards_checked: No authentication, no HMAC/signature on state, no class allow-list, no type check before Marshal.load. Exploitability depends on gadget classes loaded at runtime, which cannot be verified from this repository (no Gemfile).

verdict.guard_found: none. app.rb:5 is an unauthenticated `post "/restore"` route with no before filter or auth helper. app.rb:6 calls `Marshal.load(Base64.decode64(params[:state]))` with no HMAC/signature check, class allow-list, or type check. app.rb:7 returns `state.inspect` to the caller. Sinatra merges query and form params, so `params[:state]` is attacker-controlled. The only gap is that code execution depends on gadget classes loaded at runtime, which this repo cannot show.
verdict.reason: The route at app.rb:5 is reachable anonymously, and app.rb:6 passes attacker-supplied base64 straight into Marshal.load with no guard, so unsafe deserialization is confirmed at minimum for DoS and object-content disclosure via inspect at app.rb:7; the RCE severity depends on gadgets not visible in this repo.

finding.claim: POST /import reflects attacker-chosen JSON object key names into a text/html response without escaping, enabling reflected HTML/script injection on the app origin.
finding.source: Keys of the JSON object in the POST /import request body (app.rb:11), supplied by the client.
finding.sink: Response body from data.keys.join(",") at app.rb:12, served as text/html (Sinatra default for string responses).

trace.note: request.body.read is parsed by JSON.parse; keys are attacker-controlled strings.
keys are joined and returned unescaped as the response body.

finding.guards_checked: No HTML escaping. Possible mitigations are Sinatra default Rack::Protection (HttpOrigin would reject cross-origin POSTs with an Origin header), but config is not in the repository, so their status is unknown. Requires a victim browser to submit the crafted request.

verdict.guard_found: No in-repo guard. app.rb:12 returns data.keys.join(",") with no escaping. The only repo-visible control is none; Sinatra's default Rack::Protection stack (HttpOrigin, per framework defaults, not in this repo) may block cross-origin browser POSTs, but its state cannot be confirmed here: there is no Gemfile, config.ru, or Sinatra settings file in the directory.
verdict.reason: The trace is accurate: app.rb:11 parses the attacker-supplied JSON body and app.rb:12 returns the joined keys unescaped as a Sinatra string response (text/html by default), so a text/plain cross-origin form can deliver a JSON-valid body with HTML in a key name. Whether the framework's default HttpOrigin protection, which is not in the repository, blocks that cross-origin POST cannot be determined from the code available, so the verdict cannot be decided.

finding.claim: POST /import has no body size limit and no type check on parsed JSON, so large bodies consume memory and non-object JSON (array or scalar) raises NoMethodError at app.rb:12 (500, with backtrace shown in development mode).
finding.source: Raw request body of POST /import (app.rb:11), supplied by any client.
finding.sink: request.body.read and JSON.parse at app.rb:11 (memory use); data.keys at app.rb:12 (exception and error output).

trace.note: Entire body is read into memory and parsed without a size cap or type check.
data.keys is called without checking data is a Hash, so non-Hash JSON raises.

finding.guards_checked: None in the file. Rack/server-level body limits, if any, are not visible in the repository.

verdict.guard_found: none. app.rb:11 has no body size cap and no type check, and app.rb:12 calls data.keys without a Hash check. The file contains no before-filters, rescue blocks, or Rack/Sinatra limits. Server-level body limits (Rack/Puma/proxy) are not visible in the repo and could only reduce the memory-exhaustion half of the claim.
verdict.reason: The trace is accurate: app.rb:11 reads and parses the unbounded request body with no size or type check, and app.rb:12 calls data.keys on whatever JSON.parse returned, so a top-level array, string, number, or null raises NoMethodError and yields a 500 for an anonymous client; this is a low-severity robustness issue, and the memory-exhaustion part depends on deployment-level body limits that the repository does not show.
